Our impact is far-reaching. Because of Jesus, we can love life and be fully Alive.

Our open motto "We Live For Each Other," encompasses the foundation that Alpha Delta Pi was built on and represents our everlasting bond as sisters.

Through philanthropy, academic excellence, and dedication to service, we aim to inspire positive change.

We offer BA degrees with an emphasis in archaeology, biological anthropology, sociocultural anthropology and a general anthropology degree covering all emphasis subfields. For over half a century, the Department of Anthropology at UCSB has been an active and vibrant center of research, mentorship and teaching. We invite you to join us.

We pride ourselves in a strong collaborative research environment, an ethos maintained by our connection to several interdisciplinary research units on campus.

name: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry - Graduate Program

We aim to help students understand how messages are developed, interpreted, and exchanged to inform, influence, and connect across a wide range of social contexts and cultures.

name: Department of Earth Science

Our graduate and undergraduate students participate directly in the excitement of exploring terra incognita. Taught by a distinguished and dedicated faculty (including several members of the National Academy of Sciences, and winners of the UCSB Distinguished Teaching Award), students discover the unfolding planetary drama of which they are part.

Maintain a higher standard of learning and serve as a voice for all students.

We aim to be an indispensable resource to connect students with great opportunities and the many sources of support at UCSB that are essential for student success.

description: The LGBTQ Staff & Faculty Collective promotes a welcoming campus community for lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, and queer staff and faculty at UC Santa Barbara by providing support, resources, and events for LGBTQ employees. This collective has and will continue to seek on-going institutional support from the Resource Center for Sexual and Gender Diversity, Human Resources, and the Vice Chancellor for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

name: Library

name: Literature Club at UCSB

description: The Living Learning Communities (LLC) program fosters belonging, learning, and student success by connecting residents through shared academic, identity-based, and interest-based communities. LLCs are open to all students, and provide opportunities to engage with a variety of perspectives while building meaningful connections. This Shoreline group serves as a central hub for communication, resources, and engagement for students, Residential & Community Living staff, and campus partners.

During our weekly meetings, health professionals serve as guest speakers and literature on professional schools is provided. We strive to give back to the community by participating in community service

name: Los Ingenieros

The event brings together students from diverse academic and technical backgrounds to collaborate, learn new skills, and gain practical experience in hardware development and technology.

description: The mission of MAPAS is to create opportunities for historically underrepresented communities to engage in outdoor activities and create a community that empowers one another to discover new passions they might have not been able to otherwise. Additionally, we aim to educate one another on environmental issues and foster a sense of stewardship for the outdoors.

Our education programs provide undergraduate research opportunities, graduate student training, outreach to K-12 students and teachers, and community outreach.

name: Math Club
description: The mission of the Math Club is to foster an inclusive and supportive community where all students at all levels can enhance their understanding of mathematics and build meaningful connections. We provide opportunities for academic growth through organized study groups, speaker series, and collaborations with campus resources. Additionally, we promote community and peer interaction through club social events and games. Our mission is to educate and bring people together to celebrate Hawaiʻi’s unique history, culture, and people, while creating our own ʻohana (family) on campus. By joining us, you’ll help preserve and share the values that make Hawaiʻi special, creating connections and understanding that extend beyond the islands.

We facilitate and assist in student-based political action while maintaining a social justice focus. Throughout the academic year, we inform members with guiding and helpful insight into graduate-level education and the medical field.

We as a club want to benefit all members while producing a positive impact on the environment and all those involved with us.

name: Men* Advocating for Gender Equity
description: Men* Advocating for Gender Equity (MAGE) is an interdisciplinary group of men-identified staff and faculty at UCSB committed to personal and collective action in support of women on campus. Recognizing the existence of gender inequity, we will actively engage in targeted activities to measurably improve the climate for women across our campus. name: Mental Health Peers - CAPS
description: The mission of the Mental Health Peer Program (MHP) is to support the student body achieve academic, social, and personal success. Through the provision of mental health services, MHP strives to help ensure that students - as well as the larger campus community - remain healthy in this pursuit of success. MHP promotes the emotional well-being of students through relaxation services, psychoeducational workshops, direct peer-to-peer counseling, and stress management and academic anxiety services. The group provides comprehensive preparation for careers across various M&A fields, including investment banking, law, financial due diligence, and more.

EOP provides cultural programs that facilitate interaction/collaboration between students of all cultural/ethnic backgrounds allowing them to gain an understanding of and appreciation for similarities and differences in each other and themselves. name: Military Medicine Community
description: Our mission is to empower undergraduate students interested in military medicine by providing a dedicated platform for career exploration and professional development. We are committed to building a supportive community that connects and mentors aspiring future military medical professionals. Through collaboration and shared passion, we aim to equip our members with the knowledge and network necessary to successfully pursue a career serving our nation's heroes.

name: Mindful Mentors
description: Our mission is to introduce mindfulness practices to elementary school students, addressing the current absence of mental health education in the public school curriculum. To address this gap, we conduct 45-minute lessons focusing on teaching children effective ways to manage their thoughts and emotions. We collaborate with local schools by reaching out to teachers and volunteering in their classrooms to deliver our lessons. name: Mindfulness Club

The creation of this union allow students to connect with others who share their experiences outside the monoracial norm of most cultural student clubs.

name: Mock Trial Team at UCSB
description: Mock Trial allows undergraduate students to take on the roles of attorneys and witnesses, acting out a fictitious case while competing against the mock trial teams of other universities. You are scored not only on content but also on performance.

description: UCSB Model United Nations is a student-run organization that simulates United Nations debates. MUN encourages international awareness and develops communication skills by allowing students to take on the role of sovereign countries and individual characters in order to participate in structured debate to find solutions for global issues. Our members compete with students from other colleges and universities in conferences across the nation, in addition to hosting our own high school and collegiate-level conferences.

We want to create convenient access for international students to learn about psychological healthiness and help them to relieve their stress while studying abroad.

The club also generates its own ideas and applies for NASA grants and funding to further develop its concepts. The team is divided into sub-categories with different projects.

name: Movie Madness Monday Club

In a time where movies are consumed on streaming services and in clips viewed from our beds and couches, Movie Madness Monday Club seeks to bring the magic back to film with a intentional community oriented viewing experience.

name: Mu Delta Pre-Medical Fraternity
description: Mu Delta's mission is to provide pre-medical and pre-health students an environment in which they can succeed in pursuing their desired profession. We emphasize academic excellence, community outreach, and networking for each member so that they are prepared for life after graduation. It is our goal to instill in our members a sense of confidence and brotherhood so that the community we create for them is both academically-stimulating and supportive of their success.

name: MultiCultural Center

Such a space was intended to facilitate the retention and recruitment of students of color and to combat institutional racism and ethnocentrism. These aims were to be realized in part through educational programming, which would promote changes in attitudes and behaviors throughout the campus community. We believe that working alongside other artists and supporting each other is paramount in creating a musical community that can lead to life long connections.

name: Muslim Student Association
description: We are active on our Instagram @ucsbmsa and Groupme (link in instagram bio)! MSA is open to all who wish to attend, dedicated to increasing understanding of Islam and Muslims. A forum for Muslim students to meet and spend time together. A group devoted to encouraging each other towards good (as individuals, as a society, practically and spiritually) and educating our student body on the diversity and beliefs in the Islamic religion.

name: Naked Voices A Cappella
description: Naked Voices is a student-run, co-ed A Cappella group at the University of California, Santa Barbara. Founded in 2000, we became the first A Cappella group on campus and have since received numerous awards and recognitions. We aim to build a fun family of talented, collaborative musicians who represent UCSB by performing at competitions, TV shows, and gigs - all while forming lifelong friendships.

name: National Residence Hall Honorary

We strive to promote these values through passive and active programming in both internal and external societies, leadership development workshops, and projects aimed to benefit our community.

name: National Student Speech Language Hearing Association

The National Student Speech-Language-Hearing Association (NSSLHA) is the only student-led pre-professional organization for students interested in the fields of communicative sciences and disorders and audiology, accredited by the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). UCSB NSSLHA is dedicated to providing a support system and community for UCSB students interested in these career paths and the study of CSD or any related majors, such as linguistics and communication.

name: NEST QUEST: IV’S HOUSING AWARENESS AND CONTRACT LITERACY PROJECT
description: Nest Quest is dedicated to empowering UCSB students to make informed housing decisions by providing resources on contract literacy, tenant rights, and practical living in Isla Vista. The organization seeks to foster a supportive community where students can learn about navigating living away from home for the first time, roommates, housing markets, avoiding scams, and advocating for affordable housing solutions.

name: Neurodivergent Student Project
description: The Neurodivergent Student Project is dedicated to promoting the well-being and success of UCSB students who have autism or ADHD, or otherwise identify as being neurodivergent. The vision of the project is for neurodivergent students to support each other in a community of peers, mentors and coaches, and to build bridges with the larger school community to create more understanding and inclusion through events and activities.

description: The Neuroscience Club at UCSB (NeuroUCSB) aims to create a supportive community for students passionate about neuroscience, fostering connections across disciplines. name: Non-competitive Soccer
description: Mission: Competitive soccer practice for the community of soccer players at UCSB.

description: The Non-Traditional Student Resource Center provides a community space for students whose life experiences may differ from traditional students. name: Nursing Club UCSB
description: To provide education on the nursing profession for all those interested. To provide networking opportunities related to the healthcare & medical field. To create a welcoming environment and community for all majors and grades at UCSB. There is no one right path to nursing.

description: To work on software that supports students in leasing, subleasing, and connecting with housemates for off-campus housing.

name: Off The Grid
description: Off The Grid strives to create and cultivate a community network dedicated to supporting women in the outdoors. We aim to encourage engagement and leadership in the outdoor community by creating club outings, events, and clinics that are focused on introducing and increasing the skills, knowledge, connections, and support necessary for women to reach their full potential in the natural world.

name: Office of Black Student Development
description: In response to a strong culture of Black student activism, the Office of Black Student Development (OBSD) advances the experiences of all Black students, advocates for their needs, and fosters their personal and academic achievement through graduation and beyond. Through the development of innovative and sustainable programs and services aimed to increase the recruitment, retention, academic achievement, holistic support, and self-advocacy of our Black population, OBSD addresses the needs of the Black student community and holds ourselves and the university responsible to meet those needs. name: Office of Financial Aid & Scholarships
description: The University of California, Santa Barbara Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships provides students with the financial resources and related services necessary to achieve their educational goals. We are committed to providing accurate, user-friendly, responsive, and respectful service to students and their families. We administer federal, state, and university aid and scholarship programs in accordance with applicable policies and regulations while striving to be an innovative and service-minded department.

name: Office of International Students & Scholars
description: OISS serves UCSB's international community as well as campus departments, faculty, and staff that work with international students and scholars. Our goal is to cultivate an inclusive environment which supports international students academically, professionally and personally by providing holistic advising on immigration, employment and cultural matters.

name: Office of Teaching and Learning
description: CITRAL provides seminars, research, resources, and support for equitable teaching and learning.

name: Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor
description: The Executive Vice Chancellor is committed to working with all of the UCSB constituents to chart a strategic path that positions UCSB as one of the nation's top research universities in the 21st century; one that emphasizes our commitment to the highest quality of teaching, research, public service, outreach, and the pursuit of excellence and diversity.

name: Office of the Ombuds
description: The Office of the Ombuds at UC Santa Barbara provides confidential consultation services to faculty, staff, students, parents, or anyone else with a campus-related concern. The ombuds addresses workplace issues, interpersonal conflict, academic concerns, policy questions, and many other problems, whether as a first step, last resort, or at any point along the way. The Office of the Ombuds is dedicated to ensuring fairness throughout the University and regularly makes recommendations for systemic change.

name: Office of the Registrar
description: The Office of the Registrar establishes and maintains the academic records of the University, and provides students with the enrollment services necessary to attain their educational goals. We support the mission of the University by providing accurate, responsive, respectful service through the continual development of our staff, policies, procedures, and technology.

name: Old Town Goleta Neighborhood Creek Project
description: The Old Town Goleta Neighborhood Creek Project is dedicated to restoring and protecting the creeks and waterways of Old Town Goleta through hands-on stewardship, community partnership, and education. We bring together UCSB students, local residents, and neighborhood organizations to care for our local watersheds. Together we will build a healthier environment and a more connected community, one cleanup and one relationship at a time.

name: ONDAS Student Center
description: The ONDAS Student Center at UCSB promotes the success and retention of first-generation college students with an emphasis on the first year transition and underrepresented student experience. We provide mentoring and academic support in a learning-centered space for students to connect with faculty, staff, and peers in order to grow personally and excel academically.

name: One Body SB
description: ONE Body SB serves to enhance unity between campus ministries and local churches in Santa Barbara for the purpose of shining the Fullness of God's Love. We do this through hosting and collaborating in events involving music and the arts, community service, as well as social justice.

name: One Love UCSB
description: One Love's mission is to stop relationship abuse by educating young people about healthy and unhealthy relationship behaviors and empowering them to be leaders of change in their communities. A Team One Love Club focuses on three things: facilitating workshops, leading activations (awareness building activities), and hosting fundraisers. The club will have monthly meetings to plan for these goals, learn more about the organization, and have conversations around healthy relationships.

name: out in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math

name: Pakistani Student Association

Our mission is to build a welcoming space for students of Pakistani descent and allies, where we can foster community, cultural pride, and meaningful dialogue. Through events, collaborations, and advocacy, PSA strives to empower students, embrace diversity, and cultivate leadership and cross-cultural understanding.

name: Pan-African Student Association
description: The mission of the Pan African Student Association is to raise the consciousness of Africans here at UCSB towards Pan-Africanism and to use the knowledge and skills learned on this campus for the masses of our people.

We aim to connect UCSB students with learners who may have limited access to educational resources and help empower them to pursue their academic and personal goals.

name: Partners in Health UCSB
description: Our mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. By establishing long-term relationships with sister organizations based in settings of poverty, Partners In Health strives to achieve two overarching goals: to bring the benefits of modern medical science to those most in need of them and to serve as an antidote to despair. We draw on the resources of the world’s leading medical and academic institutions and on the lived experience of the world’s poorest and sickest communities. name: Partners in Wellness

PATH is a local homeless shelter that is "dedicated to helping individuals, families, and communities end their homelessness." Specifically, the organization will collaborate with PATH Santa Barbara's volunteer coordinator to assist with volunteering at the site and fundraising off-site, with personal growth and the development of compassion within the students involved being at the forefront of our mission.

name: Peer Education Network

Foster communication between departments to increase effectiveness of services/programming and reduce silos. Complete critical division-wide training sessions. Encourage campus partners to offer additional training sessions outside of training week.

POP offers a community for polynesian students and an educational space for those interested in learning about the culture.

The organization also serves to host an annual retreat, as well as an annual Nowruz show celebrating the Persian New Year.

description: Pre-Law Society at UCSB seeks to create an environment where students can expand their knowledge of the legal profession while connecting members with resources to enhance their chances for law school admission. In addition, the society seeks to improve and expand UCSB pre-law culture through providing members with professional help and guidance.

Our mission is to provide a platform for education, networking, and professional development through engaging events, industry insights, and collaboration with experienced professionals. We strive to empower our members with the knowledge, skills, and connections necessary to excel in the fields of finance and investment management, and to create a supportive community that encourages early-stage career growth.

description: This organization's purpose is: To supply resources and support for students seeking internships and other professional industry opportunities after graduation. To encourage confidence and other interpersonal skills for career preparation and discovery. To provide equitable access to career opportunities. To foster a close-knit community among physics students.

description: The purpose of the Professional Fraternity Council is to facilitate collaboration and communication between the various member fraternities who make up the Council and to collectively represent the needs of those fraternities. name: Professional Women's Association

Project Moonlight UCSB will give students the opportunity to get involved with this nonprofit in a large variety of ways. Members will have the chance to receive EMS training, participate in outreach and planning, and go abroad on life changing trips to teach communities.

name: Project Room Bloom

By engaging UCSB students in meaningful service, we aim to brighten residents’ living spaces, foster intergenerational connection, and create small moments of joy, individuality, and belonging.

Show them how to notice early signs of certain eye conditions and diseases. - Increase better access to eye care for university students and underserved communities.

name: Prose and Cons
description: We are a creative writing club filled with members who work to encourage and help one another in various writing projects. We host weekly meetings where members can bring in their individual pieces for workshopping, as well as writing sprints where all writers can set time out of their day to write during their busy lives. Our goal is to have fun together and support each other in improving our craft!

name: Psi Chi, The International Honor Society in Psychology

description: Our mission is to invite students, specifically those with a significant interest in mental health, to partake in volunteer opportunities guided toward supporting those struggling with psychological disorders.

name: Psychedelic Club of UCSB
description: Our mission is to increase mainstream cultural awareness and acceptance of psychedelics. We are here to promote open and honest psychedelic expression and reduce the stigma, shame, and fear associated with such expression. We hope to facilitate educational conversations about psychedelics and present accurate, unbiased information on these substances. The club will be an academic space for students to explore psychedelic research and the therapeutic potential of psychedelics. Here is a link to our Discord if you would like to join the discussion! https://discord.com/invite/WBKeZAC

name: Psychic Academy

We are dedicated to creating enrichment toys for donation, organizing hikes and beach outings to provide shelter dogs a day out of the shelter, and promoting adoption efforts to connect animals with loving families. Through our passionate efforts, we strive to improve the overall welfare of shelter animals, advocating for their well-being and enriching their lives while they await their perfect match.

name: Quantitative Biology Club @ UCSB
description: Provide supplemental resources to students at UCSB interested in quantitative biology.

name: Queer and Trans Graduate Student Union

We will also advocate for the rights and well-being of LGBTQQIA+ identified students and will provide mentorship to undergraduate students. Furthermore, the Union will work to foster ties with the LBGTQQIA+ community in the greater Santa Barbara area.

Ravaani's goal is to make the a cappella experience fun, unique, and raw and promote South Asian cultural awareness across campus. We hold large ministry-wide gatherings as well as small bible studies for students based on their class.

Furthermore, we hope to give members opportunities towards their steps to the film industry in directing, producing, cinematography, editing, casting, marketing, and much more!

name: Student-Initiated Outreach Program (SIOP)
description: The Student Initiated Outreach Program (SIOP) empowers Registered Campus Organizations (RCO) to participate in student-led outreach to inspire, motivate, and guide historically underrepresented and income-eligible, pre-college youth and transfer students. description: Students Against Poverty at UCSB aims to support the global mission of the nonprofit organization Moms Against Poverty of “lessening the incidence and effects of poverty for impoverished children around the world” by raising awareness, engaging in community outreach, and organizing fundraising events.

name: Students for Inclusivity and Diversity in Environmental Studies
description: The mission of SIDES is to uplift and support minority/underrepresented students who are majoring in Environmental Studies.

name: Students for Justice in Palestine at UCSB
description: Students for Justice in Palestine at UCSB is a group of undergraduate and graduate students working toward justice and the recognition of universal rights for all current and displaced residents of historic Palestine. We stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people's struggle for self-determination, justice, and equality. name: Students Supporting Israel

name: Successful Student Transitions

name: Summer Research Academies
description: The Summer Research Academies offer a dynamic, 4-week summer program that introduces qualified high school students to the research enterprise through project-based, directed research in STEM, Humanities, and Social Sciences fields.

name: Summer Sessions
description: During seven sessions of varying length (from the end of June to mid-September), Summer Sessions offers over 600 courses, including online courses, and works with faculty and departments to develop unique learning experiences in special courses and programs well suited to the summer term. Summer Sessions makes it possible for students to get a head start and to make progress toward their degree year-round, with financial aid and housing available. name: Sunrise Santa Barbara
description: Sunrise Santa Barbara is a local hub of the national Sunrise Movement whose mission is to put everyday people at the forefront of the climate revolution and build a sustainable world that works for all of us, now and for generations to come.

name: Supporting Epilepsy Awareness
description: The mission or purpose of Supporting Epilepsy Awareness (SEA) is to advocate, educate, and spread awareness to our community and all individuals around us about epilepsy, how to care for someone who has or is having a seizure, and what the common signs and symptoms to look out for are. It will also provide a safe space to share stories, communicate, share ideas about how to raise awareness for epilepsy, and simply be a community that supports one another and our journeys.

name: Surf Club at UCSB
description: To cultivate a strong community where members of all skill levels can come together to develop their abilities and foster friendships in and out of the water.

name: Surfing Team

name: Swifties of UCSB
description: Our mission is to bring together and create a community of people who love Taylor Swift here on campus.

name: Swim Team

Creating an organized, competitive team will foster the swimming community at UCSB and give students an opportunity to bond with like-minded people, and will connect students to the campus in a positive way.

name: Swing & Ballroom Dance Club
description: To promote and encourage social dancing, social dance etiquette and the fun that accompanies it, on campus and in the community, by serving as a resource for dances and dancing.

We also administer course evaluation surveys, support and maintain classroom technology, and run the campus video studios. We foster a climate for excellence in instruction at UCSB.

Together, we strive to raise cultural awareness through various social and cultural activities throughout the year.

name: The Center for Science and Engineering Partnerships
description: The mission of the Center for Science and Engineering Partnerships (CSEP) is to strengthen UCSB's capacity to play a leading role in the education and professional development of current and future scientists and engineers.
